 There’s a quick turn-around following Saturday’s 1-1 draw against Union Berlin, with FC Augsburg set to face SG Sonnenhof Großaspach in the second round of the DFB-Pokal on Tuesday evening (18:00 CET).  
 The third-division side caused an upset in the first round of the competition, knocking Arminia Bielefeld out after a penalty shootout. Despite SGS’s recent 7-1 loss against Wehen Wiesbaden in the league, Manuel Baum is wary of the dangers they can pose. “In Großaspach, we’re up against a team who play with intensity and want to play football,” said the FCA head coach, adding that it has been “very interesting to see how they’ve been performing in the third division.”
 The 47-year-old is already aware that cup games are different from the average match. “Games in the Pokal are always something special and you really look forward to being involved in them,” explained Baum. Following the 2-0 victory against Energie Cottbus in the first round, FCA are now looking to build on their success. “We want to play with high intensity and give it everything we’ve got,” emphasised the head coach. 
 Brackelmann set to miss out 
 Noahkai Banks, Steve Mounié and Alexis Claude-Maurice all remain sidelined. Calvin Brackelmann was allowed to return home from the hospital on Saturday evening, but his concussion means he too will miss Tuesday’s game. Luckily, Baum explained that, “he’s doing well given the circumstances.”
 There’s positive news regarding Juma Bah, though, who will be eligible to play in the cup tie following his red card against Union Berlin. Baum has been extremely clear in relation to the racist remarks targeted towards Bah, saying, “We will not look the other way in situations like this. We will stand even more united and respond immediately.” He described the club’s handling of the racist comments that had been posted publicly on the player’s Instagram page as “sensational”. Bah felt “that he had our full support”, said Baum.
